files.why: Generic date-range filter control for the invoice list; duplicated in-slice per rule 7 (this is only the 2nd same-reason usage, not yet 3), zero domain nouns in name/props.
Mount the filter at the top of the invoices card and bind the selected range.
Own the date-range state and filter the cached invoices by it (client-side, matching the existing cache-store pattern).
Twin generic filter control for the day view — identical look/behaviour, duplicated rather than shared per rule 7.
Mount the filter at the top and drive the range instead of the hardcoded single demo day.
Accept a date range instead of a single Date ref and load appointments across it.
Add a range query (fetchAppointmentsForRange); today only fetchAppointmentsForDay exists (isSameDay).

uncertain: shared/ vs duplicate: README worked example 3 headlines a date-range picker at shared/ui/date-range-picker/, but constitution rule 7 says promote only at the 3rd same-reason usage — this is the 2nd, so I duplicated one component per slice. 'Same look and behaviour in both' pulls hard toward sharing immediately; that's a genuine architecture-review call. If the team elects to share now, the two .vue files collapse into shared/ui/date-range-picker/{DateRangePicker.vue,index.ts} instead.

Billing filtering placement: I kept the range filter client-side in useInvoiceList over the already-cached invoices (mirrors the store's ensureLoaded pattern). If it must hit the API with range params, billing/data/queries.ts and billing/data/store.ts change too.
The DateRange value type ({start,end}) placement: left inline in each slice's component/composable to avoid a premature shared surface; it could instead live in shared/lib as a domain-free type.
questions: Which invoice date should the range filter on — issueDate, dueDate, or the 'Generated from' appointment start shown in the list column? They differ and the current list only displays the appointment date.

The day view is single-day by design (fixed demo day, day-scoped conflict highlighting). Should a date range turn it into a multi-day view, or just choose which single day is shown? How should conflict detection behave across a multi-day range?
What are the default range and the cleared/empty behaviour (e.g. default to today or current month; show everything when cleared)?
Should the selected range be reflected in the URL/query params (persist across reload/navigation) — which would also touch each slice's routes.ts — or is component-local state fine?
Is client-side filtering over already-fetched data acceptable, or must filtering hit the mock API with range parameters (affecting data/queries.ts and the MSW mocks)?
